welcome.sub:
Fledge gives your Claude Code a graphical workbench: manage several projects, keep work and personal accounts apart, and run multiple sessions side by side.
Next we'll walk through your development environment and settings. Every step is optional — you can rerun any of them later from Settings.

bundle.sub: Pick a backup bundle. Fledge expands it into a brand-new folder so you can see what's inside before deciding what to bring back — nothing you already have is touched in this step.

sum.note: This counts the project folders inside the bundle. On the next step, projects whose original path can't be read won't be listed, so that count may be lower.

errors.infoFailed: The bundle was expanded, but its contents couldn't be read.

targets.sub: Confirm where each account and each asset outside the accounts should go on this machine. Your settings file is created once you confirm.
targets.missingNote: A location that doesn't exist yet is fine — just connect it later (a network drive from the old machine usually isn't mounted yet).
targets.noSuggestion: The old location wasn't under the home folder, so fill this one in yourself.
targets.skip: Leave empty to skip this item
targets.skipNote: Items left empty won't be brought over: {{names}}
targets.needOne: Give at least one account a location.
targets.created: Your settings file has been created. Adjust it later from Settings.
targets.stale: This bundle's contents no longer match what you saw on the previous step. Go back and confirm the bundle again.

errors.loadFailed: Couldn't read landing spot suggestions for this bundle.
errors.reloadFailed: Your settings file was created — it just hasn't been read back yet. Hit “Read again” to retry; nothing gets created twice.

targets.reused: This machine already had a settings file, so it was reused instead of creating another.

adopted.note: These came from the Fledge settings inside the backup bundle. Anything whose old location doesn't exist on this machine is left out (a network drive you haven't mounted yet, for example) — you can fill it in later from Settings.

conflict.h: This machine already has a settings file
conflict.fromDest: It was created from this unpacked bundle:
conflict.fromOnboard: It came from the “Start fresh” path, not from a backup bundle.
conflict.unknown: There's no record of where it came from.
conflict.note: If you reuse it, the remaining steps will use its destinations — which may not be the ones from this bundle. If you're unsure, stop here and take a look in Settings first.

paths.sub: Whether /resume can find a conversation depends on the project's absolute path — if the path changed, it won't match. Set where each project lives on this machine.
paths.count: This bundle has {{total}} project folders; {{listed}} of them have a readable original location and can be mapped.
paths.countNote: The ones without a readable original location aren't broken: their history still comes over, it just can't be mapped to a new path automatically.
paths.missingNote: A location that doesn't exist yet is fine — the rewrite follows the path you type, so moving the project there later will line up.
paths.skipNote: Projects left empty ({{names}}) keep their history as-is, but /resume won't list them unless you put the project back at its original path.
paths.none: There are no mappable projects in this bundle — just continue.
paths.note: Nothing is written on this step — the rewrite happens at install time, so you can come back and change it any time before then.

errors.loadFailed: Couldn't read the project list for this bundle.

paths.shared: This path exists in each of these accounts; the rewrite applies to all of them:

install.sub: Before you install, see exactly what will happen. Nothing is written on this step.
install.atLeastNote: Links inside account folders aren't in this number, so the final count can be higher than shown — that's normal, not an error.
install.willSkip: Skipped (something is already there; nothing is overwritten)
install.blockedNote: These locations are occupied by a regular file or a link, so nothing can go underneath them. Clear what's in the way and run this again — they'll move to “will be brought over”.
install.excludedExtraNote: Each of these may be a large bundle of files. To bring them over, go back a step and give them a location.
install.renames: Projects whose paths will be rewritten
install.unmapped: Projects with no mapping — moved as-is
install.missingAccounts: Accounts in this bundle that you gave no location
install.missingAccountsNote: Not one byte of these accounts will be moved. To bring them over, go back a step and give them a location — the preview won't mention them again.
install.none: There's nothing to bring over this time.
install.runNote: Installing — please leave this window open. This step writes into your account folders for real.

errors.loadFailed: Couldn't work out what this install would do.
errors.installFailed: This install never started — nothing was touched.
errors.installUnknown: No result came back, so there's no telling how far it got — whatever was already written may well have completed. Pressing install again is safe: files already in place are never overwritten, and they show up as “skipped”.
errors.resumeFailed: Couldn't pick up the last migration — that expanded bundle can't be read right now. Choose and expand a bundle again, then rerun the wizard.

sub.ok: This install finished. Here's what happened, item by item.
sub.partial: Some items didn't make it. Here's what happened, item by item — the ones that failed show why.
sub.allSkipped: Nothing was written this round: every destination already had a file of the same name, and those are never overwritten. Only the name is compared, never the contents, so there's no guarantee what's there came from this bundle — an earlier round that already finished looks the same.
sub.none: Nothing was brought over this time. Here's why each item didn't make it.

result.skipped: Skipped (something was already there; nothing is overwritten)
result.moreNote: “Brought over” can be higher than the preview on the last step: links inside account folders aren't in that number. A higher count is normal, not an error.

reason.read_only_filesystem: that location is on a read-only disk
reason.cross_device: source and destination are on different disks
reason.operation_not_supported: that disk doesn't support this operation
reason.source_moved: the bundle changed mid-install (moved, deleted, or swapped for another)
reason.target_moved: the landing spot was swapped mid-install
reason.overlapping_config_dirs: two landing spots point at the same place
reason.provenance_unavailable: this migration's record couldn't be read, so it stopped here to be safe
reason.account_not_installed: this account itself didn't install, so its links weren't created
reason.node_identity_mismatch: what the link points to was swapped before it could be created
reason.not_migrated_by_design: deliberately not moved (set this up again on the new machine)
reason.not_a_regular_file: not a regular file (pipe, device node, etc.) — not moved
reason.symlink_target_unauthorized: nothing it could point at came over in this round, so it wasn't recreated (a link already in place is untouched)

stale.h: Also found {{count}} temporary files left by an interrupted run
stale.note: They're left over from a migration that was interrupted. They don't affect how Claude runs, and you can delete them yourself.

repair.sub: A backup bundle stores the links themselves, not the files they point at — after moving to this machine they still point at the old machine's paths. This step re-points them at the matching locations here.
repair.scope: Only links whose target no longer exists get rebuilt. Links that point somewhere else but still work are left alone — you may have set those up on purpose. Anything that would overwrite existing content is skipped; handle those from the “Dev environment” section in Settings, where you can approve them one by one.

login.why: Credentials are deliberately kept out of backup bundles, so this step can't be skipped — what came back is your settings and data, not your signed-in state.

roots.sub: Each root folder's immediate subfolders are scanned as projects.
roots.note: Your settings file is created when you finish this step. Everything after this is optional — close the window whenever you like and the root folders you added are kept. Pick up the rest from Settings.
roots.created: Your settings file has been created. Root folders can be adjusted in Settings from now on.

env.sub: Install anything that's missing right here, then hit Re-check to refresh.
env.brewHint: The official installer is interactive and needs sudo — please run it in your own terminal.
env.installHint: Stay on this step while it installs — leaving cancels the install.
env.pathHint: PATH and git identity: ~/.local/bin must be on your PATH (claude and uv install there); commits fail if git config --global user.name/user.email is unset. Neither is detected automatically in this version.

login.sub: Each account signs in separately — shared config files do not carry your login.
login.note: Fledge cannot confirm whether a sign-in succeeded: on macOS, Claude keeps its credentials in the Keychain rather than the account's config directory. All we do here is open a terminal with the right account environment — check its output to see how it went.
login.codexDesc: Codex signs in globally, not per account.
login.leaveHint: Stay on this step while signing in — leaving closes the terminal and cancels it.

cc.sub: Let both accounts use one copy of commands, plugins, skills and settings instead of maintaining each side separately.
cc.ownerDesc: {{target}} gets links pointing at {{source}}'s matching items. CLAUDE.md stays a real file on both sides.

state.broken_link: the link's target no longer exists
state.real_dir: you have your own folder, and it isn't empty
state.content_differs: you have your own version, contents differ
state.source_unsupported: {{source}}'s copy of this item can't be shared

cc.excludedHint: These accounts are left out this time — their config folders don't exist or can't be used: {{accounts}}. Check those accounts' config folders in Settings.
cc.conflictHint: Anything marked “Left as is” stays untouched — setup only does things that can't overwrite your work. To switch to {{source}}'s version, open the Development environment section in Settings, where you can authorise each item individually (it renames a backup first).
cc.advHint: The advanced item projects (shared session history) is left alone by default.
cc.nothingToDo: Nothing to do — these items are already the way you want them.
cc.naDesc:
{{path}} doesn't exist — you're using a single account, so there's nothing to share.
This card reappears once you add a second account in Settings.
cc.naDescBlocked:
We couldn't confirm whether {{path}} can serve as another account's config folder, so this step is skipped (we won't touch a folder we haven't confirmed).
Check that account's config folder in Settings.
cc.naDescSingle:
Only one account is registered, so there's no second account to share settings with.
This card reappears once you add another account in Settings.

sys.sub: All three are optional and can be changed any time in Settings.
sys.subsDesc: Used by the dashboard to work out net return (cost vs usage).
sys.kmsDesc: The memory panel reads library/ and topics/ under this folder as cross-project knowledge.

project-starter.name: Project starter
project-starter.desc: A CLAUDE.md and docs/ skeleton for a new project — generic, meant to be edited.

kms-seed.name: Second brain
kms-seed.desc: A research and ideation vault: CLAUDE.md rules, topics/ and library/ templates, derived index files, and Claude Code hooks for session wrap-up.

result.conflict: Name taken by a different kind of item — left alone

sys.deployHint: Never overwrites: existing files at the destination are always kept, only what's missing is added.

done.summary:
Found {{projects}} projects
across {{roots}} root folders and {{accounts}} accounts
done.hint: Anything you skipped — sign-in, templates — is waiting in the Development environment section of Settings.
done.migHint: Once you're signed back in you're ready to go. Your conversation history came along with each account directory — run /resume inside a project to find it. Projects you left unmapped are the exception: Claude Code won't list their history (the files are still on disk).
done.migCaveats: Two things rebuild themselves over time: your tool permission list and MCP settings didn't come along (they live in the same file as machine identity and caches, and moving that file wholesale would wipe the state you just signed in to). Normal use fills them back in.
done.migSummaryUnknown: Migration finished. One install round never reported back, so there's no item count here — the install results page on the previous step is the accurate record.

st.backupHint: Ticked items are renamed to {{name}} before the link is created — nothing is deleted outright.
st.rerunHint: Environment checks and sign-in are one-off steps — <rerun>rerun setup</rerun> whenever you need them.

errors.denied: Some folders couldn't be read — grant access in System Settings
errors.scan_failed: Scan failed — try again in a moment
errors.onboard_failed: Couldn't save your settings — try again in a moment
errors.status_failed: Couldn't check your tools — try again in a moment
errors.unknown_install_id: No install command is available for this tool — please install it manually
errors.install_failed: Couldn't start the install — try again in a moment
errors.projects_reload_failed: Your settings were saved, but the project list failed to load — try again in a moment
errors.unknown_account: That account no longer exists — check your account settings
errors.login_failed: Couldn't open the sign-in terminal — try again in a moment
errors.check_dir_failed: Couldn't check the account's config folder — try again in a moment
errors.common_config_failed: Couldn't apply the shared settings — please try again
errors.config_not_initialized: Your settings file doesn't exist yet — finish the work folders step first
errors.config_unreadable: Fledge's settings file is missing or damaged — check ~/.fledge/config.json
errors.probe_failed: Couldn't read the account's config folder — grant access in System Settings and retry
errors.invalid_config_dir: An account's config folder path isn't valid — fix it in Settings
errors.unsafe_config_dir: An account's config folder points at your home folder itself, which is unsafe — pick a dedicated subfolder in Settings
errors.target_equals_source: Two accounts point at the same config folder — fix it in Settings
errors.duplicate_target: Several accounts point at the same config folder — fix it in Settings
errors.overlapping_account_dirs: The accounts' config folders contain one another — give each its own folder in Settings
errors.subs_cost: Monthly cost must be a non-negative number
errors.subs_failed: Couldn't save the subscription list — try again in a moment
errors.kms_failed: Couldn't save the knowledge base root — try again in a moment
errors.kms_failed_subs_saved: Saved the subscription list, but couldn't save the knowledge base root — try again in a moment
errors.backend_unavailable: The backend isn't connected yet — try again in a moment
errors.unknown_template: That template no longer exists — reload the list
errors.template_unavailable: This build doesn't bundle that template
errors.invalid_destination: That destination path isn't valid — pick another
errors.unsafe_destination: The destination can't be your home folder itself or one of its parents — pick a dedicated folder
errors.probe_dest_failed: Couldn't read the destination folder — check its permissions and try again
errors.template_failed: Couldn't deploy the template — try again in a moment
errors.templates_failed: Couldn't load the template list — try again in a moment
